hook: A former pet cemetery in Florida turns out to hold human bodies, and the headstones line up with the prime ministers of Montenegro. Most of the article is a single table, so read it row by row instead of skimming. It names real Montenegrin politicians and attaches dates of death, some of them still hidden, to living people.
whyItMatters:
2072 tells a story almost entirely through a list, and the list is where all the movement happens. It starts with documented political history and then slides, one gravestone at a time, into a future the Foundation can only cover up.

The containment logic is unusual too: the danger is not the bodies but the information on the stones, so staff who accidentally read the future rows are given amnestics, and the cemetery's accuracy is checked by digging up a grave whenever the office changes hands.
thingsToNotice:
Each term in office gets its own grave, which is why one man with four separate terms keeps turning up, every body genetically identical. The subtitles first read like wry political nicknames, then drift: a schoolchild who will become the Murderer of Two, a woman with gouged-out eyes, three Heretics buried only in natural fabrics, and a Superior Man rebuilt with metal prosthetics and an unnaturally long life.

After that come two stones titled Godhead with a coffin full of pure silicon and no body, and then a blank stone over an empty coffin, all listed without comment. The last row loops back to the first prime minister, with a death date earlier than the births of the men who came before him on the list.
